title: Overnight Praline French Toast Bake
changes_from_base: Bread slices sit on a buttery brown sugar and honey glaze, soak overnight in a cream custard and bake as one dish; each piece is turned over so the praline glaze ends up on top.
summary: Slices of bread baked over a sticky brown sugar glaze until golden and bubbling, finished with toasted pecans.

ingredients.item: soft light or dark brown sugar, packed
French or Italian loaf, sliced 1.3 cm thick, enough to cover the dish in one layer (about 450 g)
whipping cream (or whole milk for a lighter custard)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Melt 113 g butter in a small pan, stir in 213 g brown sugar and 2 tbsp honey, and simmer until the sugar dissolves, then pour into a buttered 23 x 33 cm dish.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Lay enough 1.3 cm thick loaf slices over the glaze to cover the dish in a single layer.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk 340 ml whipping cream with 5 eggs, 2 tsp vanilla and ¼ tsp salt, then pour over the bread, pressing it down.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate overnight, up to 24 h.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Sprinkle ¼ tsp nutmeg and ¼ tsp cinnamon over the top, then bake at 175 °C (155 °C fan) for 40-45 min until bubbling and the centre reads 71 °C.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Turn each slice over so the syrupy side faces up and scatter with 47 g toasted chopped pecans.

tips: A crusty loaf gives more chew, while soft sandwich bread makes a softer bake.
Day-old bread works well here, soaking up the custard without falling apart.
Turning the slices over before serving shows off the sticky praline glaze underneath.
storage: Best served the day it's baked; cover and keep in the fridge for up to two days, reheating in the oven to re-crisp the top. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
